claims.text: Adding approximately 5 at.% Pd and applying an optimized heat treatment will induce nanoscale Pd-rich regions in the HEA.
Nanoscale Pd-rich regions tailor local magnetic interactions.
The Pd-rich regions facilitate magnetic domain-wall motion.
The Pd-rich regions improve magnetic exchange interactions.
Facilitated domain-wall motion and modified exchange interactions produce a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
The proposed Pd addition and heat treatment preserve rapid heat exchange.
The proposed Pd addition and heat treatment maintain low magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed Pd addition and heat treatment maintain mechanical stability.
Annealing at approximately 400°C for 1 hour is expected to promote nanoscale Pd-rich segregation.
Pd-rich regions reduce energy barriers for domain-wall motion.
Lower domain-wall energy barriers reduce magnetic hysteresis.
The Pd-rich microstructure promotes rapid heat equilibration.
Microstructural refinement caused by the treatment preserves mechanical integrity.
The treated Pd-doped alloy will improve magnetocaloric temperature change per tesla by more than 10% relative to the control.
The treated Pd-doped alloy will exhibit lower magnetic hysteresis than the control.
The treated Pd-doped alloy will show no degradation, or a slight improvement, in thermal performance.
The treated Pd-doped alloy will show no degradation, or a slight improvement, in mechanical performance.
The undoped baseline is known to have a moderate magnetocaloric effect and higher hysteresis.

The hypothesized behavior should hold for nearby transition-metal-based rare-earth-free HEA compositions at approximately 5 at.% Pd, annealing temperatures of about 350–450°C, and applied fields below about 2 T.
The comparison should measure magnetocaloric response, hysteresis, mechanical strength, thermal transport, and Pd-rich nanoscale features under matched conditions.
